companies.name: Boom Supersonic
companies.context: Broke the sound barrier in January and February 2025 with no audible sonic boom on the ground, achieved via a software and physics simulation fix using weather data and ray tracing algorithms; targeting 2029 for first commercial passenger flight. Built XB1 test jet with just 50 people.

topics.name: OpenAI Codex Launch
topics.summary: OpenAI launched Codex, a cloud-based software engineering agent powered by fine-tuned O3 that handles complete coding tasks on large codebases in parallel, with PRs delivered without the user writing code; rolling out to Pro, Enterprise, and Teams users in ChatGPT with API access planned.

topics.name: Meta Llama 4 Behemoth Delay
topics.summary: Meta delayed its 2T parameter Llama 4 Behemoth model due to poor internal performance, massive researcher exodus (11 of 14 leaving), AI leadership reorganization, and admitted benchmark gaming; highlighted over-reliance on pure scaling laws without sufficient post-training investment.

topics.name: AI Scaling Laws and S-Curves
topics.summary: Discussion of how pure pre-training scaling has hit diminishing returns; industry is shifting compute allocation toward post-training, reinforcement learning, and test-time compute; technology progress reframed as a series of S-curves rather than one continuous exponential.

topics.name: Apple vs Epic Games App Store
topics.summary: Apple allegedly blocked Fortnite's return to the App Store despite court orders; Epic's Tim Sweeney accused Apple of weaponizing review processes; hosts noted Apple may be calculating that years of legal delays are worth more than complying, given five-year timeline of the original case.

topics.name: Novo Nordisk CEO Departure
topics.summary: CEO stepped down after stock fell 50% over the past year despite tripling company metrics during his tenure; GLP-1 market became hyper-competitive from other scaled pharma and compounding pharmacies; discussion of whether CEOs should be held responsible for meme stock cycles.

topics.name: US Middle East AI Infrastructure Deals
topics.summary: US struck 5-gigawatt data center deals with UAE and Saudi Arabia; analysis called them complete wins locking out China; debate over guardrails against chip resale, G42's ties to China via Lunate fund, and whether one-fifth chip allocation to G42 is too much compute for an authoritarian-linked entity.

topics.name: US-China AI Export Controls
topics.summary: Tim Fist discussed the H20 restriction costing Nvidia $5.5B, Nvidia's new Shanghai R&D center undermining the spirit of controls, Benchmark's Manus investment controversy, outbound investment restrictions, and the strategic importance of restricting both chip quality and quantity flowing to China.

topics.name: Boom Supersonic Progress and Regulation
topics.summary: Boom broke the sound barrier twice in early 2025 with no audible ground sonic boom via software fix using ray tracing and weather data; bipartisan bill to lift the 1973 US supersonic ban introduced in House and Senate with Musk and Isaacman endorsing it; 2029 target for first passenger.

topics.name: CRISPR Baby Gene Therapy Breakthrough
topics.summary: Scientists used personalized CRISPR therapy delivered via LNP doses to fix CPS1 liver disorder in a living baby — world's first personalized CRISPR therapy; designed and dosed in under six months at under $5M cost; currently applicable to single-gene mutations in accessible organs.

topics.name: Stored Series E and E-commerce Fulfillment
topics.summary: Stored raised $200M Series E, profitable for multiple consecutive quarters, shipping 30M+ packages annually to 15% of US households; tariff and de minimis changes are accelerating brand migration to their platform; robotics and AI seen as key next investment for warehouse automation.

topics.name: Substack Growth and Creator Economy
topics.summary: Substack hit 5 million paid subscriptions surpassing legacy media apps combined; subscription-aligned algorithm differs fundamentally from time-on-site optimization; building native live video and AI clip tools; Chris Best argued the creator economy trend is durable even if VC hype was misallocated.

topics.name: Open Source AI Geopolitics
topics.summary: Debate over whether the US needs a dominant open source AI stack to prevent countries from defaulting to Chinese AI infrastructure; stickiness of open source questioned since developers switch models frequently; US advantage likely comes from proving superior security, reliability, and trustworthiness.

topics.name: Hard Tech Fundraising and Build Strategy
topics.summary: Blake Scholl argued hardware companies are not uniquely capital-intensive versus internet businesses; key is finding capital-light validation methods like pre-orders since you cannot ship the product as a test; tiny focused teams (50 people built XB1) dramatically outperform bloated organizations.

topics.name: ChatGPT Sycophancy Rollback
topics.summary: OpenAI rolled back a GPT-4.0 update causing excessive user validation including in serious mental health contexts; team built new evals, identified root causes across multiple combined factors, and published two postmortems; Kevin Weil emphasized transparency as core to response.

topics.name: AI in Healthcare and Healthbench
topics.summary: OpenAI open-sourced Healthbench benchmark to improve ChatGPT's medical answering quality; Kevin Weil shared personal story of ChatGPT providing 72 hours of peace of mind about his son's surgery results while waiting to reach a doctor; framed as democratizing access to medical knowledge.

topics.name: AI Policy and Washington DC Literacy
topics.summary: Tim Fist expressed consistent disappointment at lack of AGI-aware thinking in DC even with current capabilities; argued US needs DARPA-scale basic R&D investment in AI like it did for ARPANET; highlighted the American Science Acceleration Project congressional coalition as a positive step.

topics.name: AI Social Engineering and Cybersecurity
topics.summary: Discussion of whether LLMs are enabling mass social engineering attacks; noted LLMs have exceeded average phishing quality since GPT-3.5 but mass campaigns have not been widely reported; Coinbase data breach cited as possible catalyst for increased social engineering activity.

topics.name: Public.com Synthetic Portfolio Backtesting
topics.summary: Public.com launched backtesting for synthetic portfolios; bald CEOs returned 433% vs 150% S&P; highly-paid CEOs returned 2000% vs 176% S&P; Founders Fund public portfolio returned 659%; F1 sponsor companies returned 317%; results framed as investment entertainment, not advice.

topics.name: Supersonic Flight Regulation Reform
topics.summary: A 1973 US ban prohibits exceeding Mach 1 over US soil as a speed limit not a sound limit; bipartisan bill introduced in House and Senate to lift it; Elon Musk and Jared Isaacman endorsed it; some believe Senate passage could be unanimous though hosts were skeptical.
